section.title: Rexx Code Called from Python
section.para: You want to give Python a function written in Rexx: a sort key, a function to map, an object to call.

How it works. A Rexx object passed to Python goes by reference: in Python it is an oorexx.RexxObject. Calling it sends it the message CALL, so a Rexx Routine (.context~package~findRoutine("byLength")) works wherever Python wants a function. Python's acct.balance() sends the Rexx message BALANCE to the Rexx object. A Rexx string is not an object to Python: it goes as a str, so Python's o.upper() is str's.
The routines' arguments and results cross by the usual rule: the Rexx length goes back to sorted as an int.
See also Reference, Values and RexxObject Class.

section.title: Rexx Threads and Python Threads
section.para: You want Rexx threads that call Python, and a Python thread pool that calls Rexx.

How it works. Any Rexx thread may use Python, and any Python thread may call Rexx. Each runtime has a global lock, Python's GIL and ooRexx's kernel lock, and the bridge never holds one while waiting for the other: while Python works, other Rexx threads run, and while Rexx works, other Python threads run. So four Rexx threads (START) can call Python at once, and four threads of Python's pool can call the same Rexx routine at once. This needs ooRexx 5.3.0: 5.2.0 crashes when an interpreter is used from several threads at once.
cf~ThreadPoolExecutor(4) calls the class with an argument, which makes an instance, as ~new(4) would.
